subject: Post-demo recap: candidate models, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber To: Elena Park Cc: Marissa Cole , Stephanie Nguyen , Dev Patel Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800 Subject: Post-demo recap: candidate models, benchmarks, and next steps Elena / Velvet team — thanks again for taking the demo today. Short recap and concrete next steps to keep the momentum going. What we covered (high level) - Goal: replace your in-house intent-normalization pipeline (VelvetCorp v1.2) with a deployed inference path that meets or exceeds current quality while reducing per-unit cost and improving latency SLAs. - Evaluation approach: run a short, reproducible 48–72 hour evaluation using your sample prompt sets + our harness, compare automatic metrics and human pass-rate on a held-out set, then decide on canary rollout. Recommended candidate models to trial (quick take): 1) redwood-3b-quant (our optimized, quantized 3B) — best cost/latency tradeoff; close to baseline after prompt tuning. 2) Llama-2-13B-8bit (community 13B) — strongest out-of-the-box quality on your intent set but higher cost and GPU memory needs. 3) Mistral-7B-instruct — very promising cost profile; may require targeted prompt rephrasing for edge cases. Preliminary numbers (internal dev run on your sample corpus) — synthetic, for discussion only: - VelvetCorp v1.2 (baseline): intent F1 0.82, human pass 92% (internal Velv benchmark). - redwood-3b-quant: intent F1 0.79–0.81 (with prompt set v1), latency 40–55ms p50 on Dedicated32 instances. - Llama-2-13B-8bit: intent F1 0.83, latency 120–160ms p50. - Mistral-7B-instruct: intent F1 0.77–0.79, latency ~70ms p50. Suggested acceptance criteria for the trial (proposal): - Automatic metric: F1 no more than 0.03 delta below baseline (VelvetCorp v1.2). - Human eval: >= 90% pass rate on critical intents. - Latency: 95th percentile below 250ms for host-facing flows, or pluggable to Dedicated SLA. Attachments and artifacts we've shared: - velvet_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt — your canonical prompt set (we used these for the run). - quick-benchmark-summary-velvet.pdf — short results and charts from the dev run. - sow-stub-velvet-redwood.docx — SOW + estimated timeline (draft). - cost-estimate-playbook.xlsx — pricing scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Next steps (recommended, owners): 1) You: confirm the 48–72h eval (we can start as soon as you share the final 1K sample set). (Elena) 2) Us: provision trial endpoints, run multi-model eval, and upload full artifact set to the Drive link. (Jonas / Dev) 3) Internal: build a short human-eval rubric for Velvet's top 20 intents and run blind review. (Marissa) 4) Commercial: prep SOW and a scoped cost estimate for Dedicated canary if acceptance criteria met. (Stephanie) Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync the week of Feb 16 to review trial results and decide on canary. Options: Tue 2/17 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2/18 14:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm a slot. Thanks — happy to chat through any of the numbers. — Jonas Weber Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference jonas@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123 Attachments: velvet_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt, quick-benchmark-summary-velvet.pdf, sow-stub-velvet-redwood.docx, cost-estimate-playbook.xlsx From: Elena Park To: Jonas Weber Cc: Velvet Analytics Procurement Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: candidate models, benchmarks, and next steps Jonas — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we greenlight the 48h run: 1) Parity: VelvetCorp v1.2 is tuned heavily on our catalog-specific phrasing. Can you confirm which model(s) you expect to meet parity on the end-to-end intent pipeline without changing our downstream mapping logic? If a change is required, what is the estimated engineering effort? 2) Private deployment: procurement wants to know if Private (VPC/on-prem) can be part of the SOW or if we have to start Hosted/Dedicated first. Any constraints we should be aware of? 3) Compliance: we need SOC 2 evidence and a list of what telemetry/logs would be retained during the eval. Procurement asked us to include that in the SOW if possible. If those answers look okay, we'll finalize the sample set and confirm the slot for the run. Also please include a ballpark cost delta vs our current infra when you send the SOW. Thanks, Elena Director of Product — Velvet Analytics From: Jonas Weber To: Marissa Cole , Stephanie Nguyen , Dev Patel Cc: Elena Park Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: candidate models, benchmarks, and next steps Team — forwarding Elena's procurement questions (quoted above). My replies below so we can align on the SOW and technical notes before Marissa/Stephanie send customer-facing artifacts. 1) Parity and expected engineering: short answer: Llama-2-13B-8bit is most likely to meet or exceed VelvetCorp v1.2 on out-of-the-box intent F1 for the current prompt set; redwood-3b-quant gets within ~0.02–0.03 after prompt tuning and targeted prompt templates for the top-20 intents. That means:
- If Velvet wants zero changes to downstream mapping: recommend Llama-2-13B-8bit for the short trial (accept higher cost/latency). - If Velvet is open to very small upstream prompt/template adjustments (we've already drafted 12 targeted rewrites in the attached prompt set), redwood-3b-quant is the most cost-effective path and can be put behind a Dedicated canary with automated fallback. Estimated engineering effort (ballpark): - Zero-downstream-change path (13B model): minimal engineering; mostly infra and integration testing — ~1–2 weeks to canary. - Prompt-adjust + quantized model path (3B): ~2–3 weeks including prompt tuning and a short blind human-eval loop to validate. 2) Private deployment: we can include Private in the SOW as an option but note the lead time is longer (access to customer VPCs, KMS integration, and on-prem validation). Typical timeline: 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals. We recommend starting with a Hosted/Dedicated trial, and if acceptance criteria are met, schedule Private onboarding as phase 2 in the SOW. We'll include the optional Private line item in the draft. 3) Compliance and telemetry: we'll attach a SOC 2 summary and a short telemetry retention plan in the SOW. For the eval we can limit logs to request/response hashes, token-level telemetry only on a sampled subset, and remove raw prompt text after the trial if Velvet requests. Procurement can opt-in to a short-term audit export. Other notes on parity thresholds we should propose back to the customer: - Automatic threshold: intent F1 >= baseline - 0.03. - Human eval: >= 90% pass on top-20 intents, with a separate threshold for high-sensitivity intents (>= 95%). - Rollout policy: canary can run at 5–10% traffic with immediate fallback to baseline model on regression. Action for us: Marissa, please incorporate these options into the SOW stub and include the Private-onboarding timeline as an optional appendix. Stephanie, please add cost delta scenarios (per-1M requests) for 13B vs redwood-3b-quant vs Dedicated. Dev, prep the eval harness and the Drive folder link. — Jonas From: Marissa Cole To: Elena Park Cc: Jonas Weber , Stephanie Nguyen , Dev Patel Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800 Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: candidate models, benchmarks, and next steps Elena — thanks for the thoughtful questions. We've attached a draft SOW and a short cost playbook (see attachments) that includes Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths and a ballpark delta vs typical self-hosting infra. High level answers: - Parity: we will run the two-pronged trial Jonas outlined. If you select the zero-change path (13B), timeline to canary is ~1–2 weeks. If you pick the cost-optimized path (redwood-3b-quant + prompt tuning), plan ~2–3 weeks. We will document any downstream mapping changes required during the blind eval so nothing is deployed without your approval. - Private: included as an optional line item in the SOW appendix with an estimated 4–8 week lead time; we will not start Private work until a commercial commitment is signed. - Compliance: SOC 2 summary and a one-page telemetry retention addendum are included in the SOW draft. For the evaluation we'll default to sampled telemetry and hashed payload storage unless you request otherwise. Proposed near-term schedule: 1) Velvet confirms sample set by EOD Wed 2/18. 2) We run 48–72h multi-model evaluation starting Thu 2/19. 3) Internal blind human-eval completed by Mon 2/23. 4) 30-min results review Wed 2/25 (we'll book after we have the run outputs). Please find the SOW stub and cost workbook attached. If these look good we can mark the run start date and I'll have Stephanie follow up with a redlined commercial if procurement requests it. Best, Marissa Cole Account Executive | Redwood Inference marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198 Attachments: sow-stub-velvet-redwood.docx, cost-estimate-playbook.xlsx
